TideLine accesses your approximate location in the background, including when the app is closed, to move your tide widget with you. Only the latest location is saved on this device. It is not sent to us or shared for advertising. Updates are occasional and can be delayed by Android. You can turn following off at any time; fixed locations and manual refresh still work.
In Android app settings, open Permissions → Location and choose “%1$s”. Approximate location is enough. You can decline and keep using a fixed location or foreground updates.
Background following is off. Your last fix is retained until you open the app or refresh.
Following is selected but paused: background location permission is missing. Turn following off and on to reopen permission setup.
Automatic following uses occasional approximate system locations. The latest saved fix is used between updates. Android battery settings and location availability can delay updates.

The widget refreshes approximately every 15 minutes; Android may delay it longer, especially during sleep or battery saving. It is not a live clock. The bottom-left time and height are from the last update. The main time line labels whole hours; short ticks mark 20 minutes in the 2–4 hour views. Background following is optional and also updates occasionally. Open the app or tap Refresh for an immediate calculation.
No web browser is available. You can still read this document in the app.
Approximate astronomical tide. Weather effects excluded.

Heights are centimetres relative to the model’s mean sea level. The middle line is zero. Right-hand marks show the next 24-hour maximum and minimum at their heights on the graph; the bottom-left time shows when its height was calculated.

Offline EOT20 ocean tide data, with all 17 constituents. Original harmonic values are stored losslessly. Astronomy tables support 2020–2040. Coastal gaps and small harbours can be unsupported; the Caspian has no EOT20 data. No accounts, advertising, tracking or forecast requests.
Contains EOT20 data by Hart-Davis and colleagues (2021), CC BY 4.0. Coastal subsetting and format conversion. Shoreline: Natural Earth, public domain. Astronomical basis: pyTMD 2.2.9, MIT.
